questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é matéria-prima?
options: Material da natureza usado para fabricar produtos
O produto pronto vendido na loja
A máquina que trabalha na fábrica
questions.answer: Material da natureza usado para fabricar produtos
questions.hint: Pense no que entra na fábrica antes de ser transformado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a principal matéria-prima do papel?
questions.hint: Ela vem das árvores.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual produto é feito a partir do leite?
questions.hint: Pense em alimentos guardados na geladeira.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: De qual matéria-prima se faz o chocolate?
questions.hint: É o fruto de uma árvore de clima quente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O algodão é usado na indústria para fazer:
questions.hint: Pense nas suas camisetas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual matéria-prima, aquecida em temperatura muito alta com outros materiais, vira vidro?
questions.hint: Ela existe em grande quantidade nas praias.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Da cana-de-açúcar se produzem:
questions.hint: Um é doce e o outro é usado como combustível.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a matéria-prima principal do aço?
questions.hint: É retirado das minas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A farinha de trigo é usada nas fábricas para fazer:
questions.hint: Pense em alimentos de padaria.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que a indústria faz?
questions.hint: Pense na palavra "transformação".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama o lugar onde a matéria-prima é transformada em produto?
questions.hint: É um prédio com muitas máquinas e trabalhadores.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual sequência mostra a transformação na ordem certa?
questions.hint: Comece pelo que vem da natureza.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a diferença entre artesanato e indústria?
options: Na indústria, máquinas produzem muitos produtos iguais
Na indústria, tudo é feito à mão, um de cada vez
questions.answer: Na indústria, máquinas produzem muitos produtos iguais
questions.hint: Pense em uma fábrica e em uma pessoa fazendo um vaso de barro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Na região do ABC Paulista, no estado de São Paulo, é muito conhecida a indústria de:
questions.hint: Pense em grandes fábricas com linhas de montagem.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Escolha um objeto da sua casa e explique de qual matéria-prima ele foi feito.
questions.hint: Pense em madeira, metal, tecido, vidro ou plástico.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Cite uma indústria da sua cidade ou região e diga o que ela produz.
questions.hint: Pense em alimentos, roupas, carros ou outros produtos fabricados perto de você.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a myth?
options: A true report about yesterday's news
A list of instructions for a game
A traditional story with heroes, gods or monsters, often explaining something about the world
questions.answer: A traditional story with heroes, gods or monsters, often explaining something about the world
questions.hint: Think about the stories of brave heroes told long ago.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a myth, what is a quest?
options: A long journey to find or achieve something important
questions.answer: A long journey to find or achieve something important
questions.hint: The hero has to go somewhere and do something difficult.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Who goes on the journey in a quest myth?
options: The villagers who stay at home
questions.hint: Who is the main brave character?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In many quest myths, what must the hero face before reaching the goal?
options: A monster or a dangerous challenge
questions.answer: A monster or a dangerous challenge
questions.hint: Think about what makes the quest exciting.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence begins with a fronted adverbial?
options: The hero reached the mountain after three long days.
The hero was brave and strong.
After three long days, the hero reached the mountain.
questions.answer: After three long days, the hero reached the mountain.
questions.hint: Look for the phrase that comes before the main part of the sentence.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the fronted adverbial in this sentence: 'Deep in the dark cave, the dragon was sleeping.'?
questions.hint: Which words come before the comma?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What punctuation mark usually comes after a fronted adverbial?
questions.hint: It shows a small pause.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which fronted adverbial tells us WHEN something happened?
questions.hint: Look for a time.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which fronted adverbial tells us WHERE something happened?
questions.hint: Look for a place.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which fronted adverbial tells us HOW something happened?
questions.hint: Look for the manner of an action.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which event usually comes FIRST in a quest myth?
options: The hero returns home as a champion
The hero is given a task and sets off
questions.answer: The hero is given a task and sets off
questions.hint: Think about how the journey begins.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which event usually comes LAST in a quest myth?
options: The hero returns home, changed or celebrated
The hero hears about the problem
The hero packs for the journey
questions.answer: The hero returns home, changed or celebrated
questions.hint: Think about the ending.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the best fronted adverbial to complete the sentence: '___, the hero finally saw the monster's lair.'
questions.hint: Which word shows that time has passed?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Heroes in myths are often given a magical object to help them. Which of these would fit a myth best?
options: A shield that makes its owner invisible
questions.answer: A shield that makes its owner invisible
questions.hint: Which one has magic?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one sentence for a quest myth that begins with a fronted adverbial. Remember the comma!
questions.hint: Start with when, where or how, e.g. a time or a place.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Invent a monster for a quest myth and describe it in 2 sentences using powerful adjectives.
questions.hint: Think about how it looks, sounds and moves.

en_read.topic: Playscripts: comparing a story and its play version

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a playscript?
options: A text written to be performed by actors
questions.answer: A text written to be performed by actors
questions.hint: Think about the theatre.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a playscript, what are stage directions?
options: Instructions telling actors how to move or speak
questions.answer: Instructions telling actors how to move or speak
questions.hint: They are not spoken out loud.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How are stage directions usually shown in a playscript?
options: At the very end of the book
questions.hint: They need to look different from the spoken lines.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a playscript, where is the character's name written?
options: At the bottom of the page
On the left, before the words they say
questions.answer: On the left, before the words they say
questions.hint: Actors need to see quickly whose line it is.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Does a playscript use speech marks around what characters say?
options: No, the character's name is written before their words
questions.answer: No, the character's name is written before their words
questions.hint: Think about how the lines are laid out.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Story: '"Help!" shouted Mia, running to the door.' Which is the playscript version?
options: Mia ran to the door and she was shouting help.
"Help!" shouted Mia, running to the door.
questions.hint: Look for the name, a stage direction and the spoken words.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does a story usually have that a playscript often leaves out?
options: A narrator describing thoughts and settings in detail
questions.answer: A narrator describing thoughts and settings in detail
questions.hint: Who tells us what is happening in a story?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the list of characters at the start of a playscript called?
questions.hint: The actors in a play are called the cast.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a play, how does the audience usually find out how a character feels?
options: From what the character says and does on stage
From footnotes at the bottom of the page
questions.answer: From what the character says and does on stage
questions.hint: The audience watches and listens.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What do we call a story that has been changed into a different form, such as a play or a film?
questions.hint: It begins with 'ad-'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A playscript is usually divided into short parts that happen in one place. What are they called?
questions.hint: A book has chapters; a play has…

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Story: 'The old castle was cold and dark, and the wind howled through the broken windows.' How would a playscript most likely show this?
options: With a short setting note at the start of the scene, e.g. 'A cold, dark castle. Wind howls.'
It cannot show the setting at all
With a long poem read by every actor
questions.answer: With a short setting note at the start of the scene, e.g. 'A cold, dark castle. Wind howls.'
questions.hint: Playscripts keep descriptions short.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why might a playwright leave out some events from the original story?
options: Because a play has limited time and must be acted on a stage
Because playwrights do not like stories
questions.answer: Because a play has limited time and must be acted on a stage
questions.hint: Think about time and space in a theatre.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which of these is a stage direction?
questions.hint: Which one tells the actor what to do?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Turn this story sentence into a line of playscript: 'Leo whispered nervously, "Is anyone there?"'
questions.hint: Name first, then a stage direction in brackets, then the spoken words.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Would you rather read a story or watch it as a play? Give one reason linked to what changes in a playscript.
questions.hint: Think about description, the narrator, actors and stage directions.

en_spell.topic: Year 3/4 statutory words: popular to purpose

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling is correct?
questions.hint: It ends like 'circular'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: po _ _ ible (it can happen).
questions.hint: The missing letters are a double consonant.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: pota _ _ es (more than one potato).
questions.hint: Words ending in -o often add -es in the plural.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: pre _ _ ure (pushing force).
questions.hint: Think of the word 'press'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: po _ _ ess (to own something).
questions.hint: This word has two pairs of the same double letter.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Choose the correct word: 'I ___ I will tidy my room after tea.'
questions.hint: Which word means you give your word?

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Choose the correct word: 'Football is a very ___ sport all around the world.'
questions.hint: Which word means liked by many people?

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word means 'something that you own'?
questions.hint: It comes from the verb 'possess'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Write the word that starts with 'pur' and means 'the reason why something is done'.
questions.hint: Say the word slowly and picture each part.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: populer → popular; potatos → potatoes; posision → position; probly → probably; promis → promise
questions.hint: Check each word from this week's list carefully.
questions.text: Last Saturday, Grandpa made his most populer dish: roast potatos. He said the secret was to keep the tray in the right posision in the oven. 'It's probly the best meal I make,' he laughed. I made a promis to help him cook again next week, and he said that was perfectly possible.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'something you own'?
questions.hint: Count the pairs of double letters.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'very likely'?
questions.hint: Think of the word 'probable'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'the reason for doing something'?
questions.hint: Both vowel sounds at the start are spelt with 'u'.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'to say you will really do something'?
questions.hint: It ends with a silent letter.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'the place where something is'?
questions.hint: The 'shun' sound here is spelt -tion.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: presure → pressure; possition → position; purpus → purpose; posible → possible
questions.hint: Look closely at double letters.
questions.text: Under a lot of presure, our team kept every player in the right possition. The purpus of the match was to score, and our coach said a win was still posible. Everyone cheered when the final whistle blew, and the shiny cup became our class's favourite possession for the whole term.

ipc.topic: How Humans Work: lungs and breathing

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which organs do we use to breathe?
questions.hint: They are inside your chest.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which gas does your body need to take in from the air?
questions.hint: Your cells need it to get energy.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which waste gas do we breathe out?
questions.hint: Plants take this gas in.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What is the name of the tube that carries air from your throat down to your lungs?
questions.hint: It is also called the trachea.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which sheet of muscle under the lungs helps us breathe?
questions.hint: It moves down when you breathe in.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What happens to your chest when you breathe in?
options: It gets bigger as the lungs fill with air
questions.answer: It gets bigger as the lungs fill with air
questions.hint: Put your hands on your ribs and take a deep breath.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What happens when you breathe out?
options: Air is pushed out and the lungs get smaller
questions.answer: Air is pushed out and the lungs get smaller
questions.hint: Think about blowing up a balloon.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why does your body need oxygen?
options: To release energy from food in your cells
questions.answer: To release energy from food in your cells
questions.hint: Think about energy.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: How does oxygen travel from the lungs to the rest of the body?
options: In the blood, pumped by the heart
questions.answer: In the blood, pumped by the heart
questions.hint: Which system carries things all around the body?

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which bones protect the lungs?
questions.hint: They make a cage around your chest.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: What happens to your breathing during exercise?
questions.hint: Think about how you feel after a race.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why do you breathe faster when you exercise?
questions.hint: Working muscles need more energy.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: At rest, Ella takes 15 breaths in one minute. After running, she takes 30 breaths in one minute. How many more breaths per minute does she take after running?
questions.hint: Find the difference.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Tom breathes 18 times every minute while resting. How many breaths does he take in 3 minutes?
questions.hint: Multiply the breaths by the minutes.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Which of these is harmful to the lungs?
questions.hint: Which one puts smoke into the lungs?

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Explain in 1–2 sentences why you breathe faster after running up the stairs.
questions.hint: Use the words muscles and oxygen.
